blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how architects and engineers create precise designs? They often use geometric constructions and loci to achieve accuracy.

blocks.markdown: In geometry, constructions involve creating figures using only a compass and a straightedge. Loci, on the other hand, refer to the set of points that satisfy certain conditions.

blocks.title: Bisector
blocks.text: A bisector is a line or segment that divides another line or angle into two equal parts.

blocks.markdown: To bisect a line segment, you need to find its midpoint. To bisect an angle, you need to create two equal angles from the original angle. Let's explore these constructions with examples.

blocks.title: Bisecting a Line Segment
blocks.prompt: How do you bisect a line segment $AB$?

steps.text: 1. Place the compass at point $A$ and draw an arc above and below the line segment.
2. Without changing the compass width, place the compass at point $B$ and draw another arc that intersects the first two arcs.
3. Draw a straight line through the points of intersection of the arcs. This line bisects the segment $AB$.

blocks.answer: The line drawn through the intersection points is the perpendicular bisector of $AB$.

blocks.markdown: Loci are useful in solving problems involving distances and angles. For example, the locus of points equidistant from two points is the perpendicular bisector of the line segment joining the points.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: When solving loci problems, visualize the conditions given and use basic constructions to determine the locus.
